findings: The added validator admits both targetId/lawId explicitly null only for House. Senate nulls, mixed null/string IDs, and omitted fields fail. Existing nonempty string identities still work for generic synthetic or future explicitly defined contracts.

Artifact loading now uses the same binding validator as the rubric, then still requires exact model/baseline contract equality, source/result SHA, projection source/review SHA, native SHA, forecast run/date/null identities, ordered protocol rows, cohort subset and explicit exclusions.

The focused test authenticates an invented House lock through the store and scores it; its one-race actual-looking House variant is rejected by the existing 435-winner/412-pair guard. The separate published House V1 metadata test hashes and parses the real current result and confirms its normalized targetId/lawId are null with 435/412 scope. It does not admit real observations or a grade.
limits: Review is of the narrow null-identity change and its data path. No actual 2026 result ledger, independently admitted House evaluation lock, or public grade was established. Parent reported 39/39 focused tests; this review inspected the code and tests without rerunning that suite.
